page.layout: One page of text. At the top, two engraved coin medallions, each with a printed legend around its rim. Below them, one text block of running text in one column, with two paragraphs. Below the text, an ornament (tailpiece) with no text. No margin notes.

main_text.l: D.N. OTHO. AVG. P.M.I.
VXOR OTHONII[?]
THEOPHANIA
OTHO iunior, siue Otho huius nominis secundus, supe-
rioris Othonis filius, patri Romanorum Imperatori succedit
anno mundi 4935. à Christo nato 973. attamen à patre iam an-
te sex annos fuerat Imperator creatus: cuius etiam opera Sara-
cenos, Græcósque Calabria expulerat. Hic mortuo patre Hen-
ricum Bauariæ Ducem nouis rebus studentem, debellauit: at-
que aduersus Lotarium Francorum Regem, qui sibi Lotarin-
giam asserebat, Galliam ingressus, fœdis populationibus eam
vastauit. At dum reuertitur, in Axonæ fluuii transitu graui in-
commodo à Fracis[?] afficitur, quibusdam ex suis militibus vor-
ticibus absorptis, pluribus ab insequente hoste interfectis.
Dum in Italiam festinat ad famam Græcorum principum, qui
Saraceno etiam milite instructi Italiam sibi vendicabant, vin-
citur: ac scapha confcensa, à piratis captus, in Siciliam ducitur:
liberatus, omnem in Beneuentanos iram, quòd signa deseruis-
sent, effundit: ciuitatem capit, spoliat, incendit. Tandem fato
concessit, cum imperasset solus post patrem annos decem. Con-
sulito Blond. lib. 3. Deca. 2. Egna lib. 3. Ab. Vrfper.
THEOPHANIA uxor huius Othonis secundi filia fuit
Nicephori Græcorum Imperatoris, quem regno pulsum, resti-
tuit, & confirmauit Otho. Vide Sup. Chro. lib. 12.

page.notes: The coin legends are printed within the engravings; the right legend's first word is uncertain on the scan. The ornament below the text is a decorative tailpiece with no text. Faint marks in the right margin near the lower text are show-through from the other side and were left out. The word "Fracis" is uncertain: it may carry an accent. Some words near the ink of the Egna citation are slightly blurred but read as printed.
